newsitem.title: USA: Louis Dreyfus increased reserves in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Louis Dreyfus increased reserves in 1996.

text.p: Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp Tuesday reported proved reserves totaling 990 billion cubic feet equivalent at year end, a net increase of 114 billion cubic feet over 1995's year-end position of 876 billion.
The company said its December 31, 1996, reserves were comprised of 849 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 23.5 million barrels of oil.
The company said it replaced over 250 percent of 1996's production volume of 75 billion cubic feet equivalent.
The present value of the future net revenues discounted at 10 percent was $1.1 billion at the end of 1996.

During the year, the company said, it drilled 305 wells, 95 percent of which were successfully completed as producers. These discoveries and extensions added 93 billion cubic feet equivalent to proved reserves, replacing 124 percent of 1996 production.
The company was also successful in acquiring 76 billion cubic feet equivalent of proved reserves, it said, noting most of these are located in western Oklahoma.

Chief executive Mark Monroe said "1996 marked the third consecutive year that we have replaced production by both strategies. With a $100 million exploration and development program budgeted for 1997, we are looking forward to another successful year for reserve growth."
